Q: connection to server on socket "/tmp/.s.PGSQL.5432" failed: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already A:

This code doesn't leak.

It also doesn't support DB concurrency, as there is no ThreadExecutor.

from celery import shared_task
from django.db import connections

from core.models import Example


@shared_task
def run_task():
    results = [
        Example.objects.get_or_create(name='example', id=1)[1] for _ in range(200)
    ]
    assert len(results) == 200
    assert not any(results)

    for connection in connections.all():
        connection.close()

Verify that we don't add 100 "stuck" SELECT statements on each call with this psql query.

SELECT COUNT(*)  FROM pg_stat_activity  WHERE wait_event = 'ClientRead' AND state = 'idle';

BTW close_old_connections() is only for rather old ones, like more than two seconds old.

Q: MVC-like design for console applications? A:

While the manual MVC patterns suggested here work, they require a lot of boilerplate. If you're looking for a modern way to keep your console UI (CLI) separated from your business logic, similar to how ASP.NET Core handles controllers, I actually built a library to solve exactly this.

I've published ConsoleMVC as NuGet, which brings a Controller/Action pattern to console apps. It handles:

  • Routing: Mapping user inputs/commands to specific methods.

  • Separation of Concerns: Keeps Console.WriteLine out of your logic.

  • Clean Syntax: It feels very familiar if you've used ASP.NET MVC.

You can check out the source and examples here: https://github.com/MateuszPodeszwa/ConsoleMVC
